en.title: Maximum Revenue from Contiguous Bouquets
en.description:
In the row of flowers, 0 is a rose and 1 is a cosmos. Three consecutive roses 000 sell for p, and one rose and one cosmos adjacent as 01 or 10 sell for q. Each flower can be used at most once, some flowers may go unused, and removing flowers to splice together new adjacencies is not allowed.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: The first line contains p q, and the second line contains a binary string s. Original bounds: 1≤p,q≤1000, 1≤|s|≤100000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 5; 5; 18. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: A prefix DP can skip the last flower or take a valid bouquet made of the last two or last three flowers, keeping the previous 3 states in a rolling array.
